title: Death Note
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Light Yagami, a bored top student, finds a notebook dropped by the death god Ryuk: anyone whose name is written in it dies. He sets out to rid the world of criminals by killing them, drawing a worldwide police hunt led by the eccentric detective L, and the story becomes a battle of wits between them (VIZ blurb via AniList; ANN review of volume 1).
life_message: Power to judge who deserves to die corrupts the one who takes it; justice belongs to accountable law, not one person's will (to verify how the ending frames it).

content.note: Killings by notebook drive the plot; ANN says they are not shown in graphic detail; MU Serial Killer/s, Death; AniList Crime, Tragedy.
ANN calls it possibly too dark for some, with a grotesque death god and gallows humor; AniList Tragedy (92), Gods.
Nothing sexual noted in the sources opened (to verify).
ANN mentions no strong language (to verify).
Protagonist described as megalomaniac and sociopathic (MU); memory manipulation (AniList); no self-harm noted (to verify).
Writing names to 'kill' and deceiving family and police are central (MU Manipulative Protagonist, Deception) (to verify).

dominant: Utilitarian vigilantism critiqued; might makes right; bleak view of death

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Rivalry of pride between Light and L, but disputes run through investigation, not personal duels (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Police and law are the counterweight to Light; Light himself seeks an imposed moral order (MU World Domination).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Light deceives his police-chief father; justice for all over family (MU blurb).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Light wants to rule as a god over a purified world (MU Megalomania).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Strategy, deduction and rules of the notebook dominate; shinigami are rule-bound, not worshipped.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Security from crime is the stated goal of Kira's killings.

folkways.japan: Japan's National Police Agency and a strong cultural respect for public order frame the hunt for Kira, and capital punishment's place in Japanese law sits behind the debate.

delivery.evidence: ANN says the volume raises questions about murder and whose lives matter without answering them.

personified.ideology: Utilitarian vigilante justice; ends justify killing
Rule of law and due process by deduction

delivery.note: The argument for and against Kira is carried by the duel of minds rather than speeches, with Light's growing ego the main signal (ANN).

winners_losers: Through most volumes Light and L trade victories; criminals and anyone in Light's way lose their lives. The VIZ blurb and ANN frame Light's ego as his undoing, so sympathy leans to lawful justice (ending to verify).
